glossary.definition: Latin term meaning 'from the beginning' or 'from inception.' In legal contexts, it is used to indicate that an act, contract, or instrument was invalid, void, or ineffective from the very start.
A shortened form of a written word or phrase used in legal citation. The NALT Guide prescribes minimal punctuation for abbreviations (e.g., NWLR, LFN without full stops).

A concise summary of a research work (thesis, dissertation, or article) providing a quick overview of the content, typically written after the research is completed. Abstracts are usually 300-400 words for undergraduates, 500-600 words for postgraduates, and 250-300 words for journal articles.

A scholarly periodical publication containing peer-reviewed articles written by researchers and professors. Under NALT Part Four, journal articles must follow specific footnote referencing and structure.

A section in the preliminary pages where the researcher expresses gratitude to individuals, groups, or institutions that supported the research work. Acknowledgements usually follow a pattern, starting with God, followed by supervisors, lecturers, friends and family. The NALT guide encourages uniformity and consistency in the acknowledgement format.
A series of law reports publishing selected judgments from Nigerian superior courts of record. Citations in NALT include the year, volume number, and starting page.

A foreign style of referencing that uses in-text citations and a reference list at the end of a research paper. The NALT guide adopts a footnote style of referencing instead of in-text citation, which differs from APA.

Supplementary materials (such as tables, charts, questionnaires, and other statistical data) that are included at the end of a research work, after the bibliography. Appendices are not numbered and are placed on separate pages after the bibliography.
The standard number system (1, 2, 3, etc.) used to number the main body of the research work, starting from Chapter One. Arabic numerals are also used for footnote numbering within the text.

A systematic list of all sources (books, journals, articles, etc.) consulted during research, arranged alphabetically by author’s surname. In a bibliography, the author's surname comes first, whereas, in a footnote, the name is written in the order it appears in the source.
A foreign citation guide that the NALT guide seeks to replace with its own indigenous citation guide.

A citation manual published by Harvard Law Review Association for legal documents in the United States. NALT's Blue Book Basic Guide represents Nigeria's indigenous counterpart adapted for Nigerian jurisprudence.

Judicial decisions that serve as a primary source of law. Cases are cited with the names of the parties in italics, the year of the report in brackets, the volume number, the part number, and the page number.

A page in the preliminary section of a thesis or dissertation that includes signed statements from the supervisor(s), external examiner, internal examiner, head of department, and dean of faculty/postgraduate studies indicating that the work has been examined and approved. The certification page is signed before and after the oral defense, with slightly different statements on each occasion.

The NALT guide recommends a specific structure for research projects. Undergraduates and Masters dissertations should be divided into five chapters while PhD theses should be divided into six chapters.

Symbols or abbreviations used to refer to sources in research writing. The NALT guide uses footnotes with Arabic numerals in superscripts to indicate sources, and has abolished the use of supra, infra, ante, contra, id, op cit, loc cit, passim, et seq, and etc. in favor of cross-references, indicated by a footnote number in square brackets, thus: [n].

The highest body responsible for the smooth functioning of the NALT. The committee is responsible for integrating the NALT manual into their local settings at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels.
The process of defining and explaining key terms and issues related to the research topic. It often includes definitions of major terms in the research topic.

A body within the legal education system that the NALT recommends should make Legal Research Methodology a core, compulsory course for final year undergraduate students and a refresher course for postgraduates.
A section in the concluding chapter of a research project outlining the original contributions the study makes to the field of law.
Latin term meaning 'in the presence of' or 'before.' Used in law reports to list the presiding panel of judges who heard a specific case (e.g., coram: Uwais CJN, Belgore, Karibi-Whyte JJSC).

A method of referencing where, instead of using ibid, the footnote number where the source was first cited is indicated in square brackets, thus: [n], allowing a return to the original footnote. This method is used in the NALT guide when a source has been cited previously, but not in the immediately preceding footnote.
Latin phrase meaning 'in fact' or 'in reality,' describing practices that exist in reality even if not officially ordained or recognized by law.
Latin phrase meaning 'according to law' or 'by right,' describing practices that are officially recognized by legal title or statute.
A page in the preliminaries where the candidate declares that the research work is original and not plagiarised. This page includes a signed statement by the candidate.
An optional page where the candidate may dedicate the research work to individuals or groups.
A research method focused on accurately and systematically describing a population, situation, or phenomenon, and often used in empirical research.

A qualitative research method that involves analysing legal rules and principles found in constitutions, statutes, case law, and other legal sources. It is also known as the conceptual or library-based approach.
Research focused on the systematic analysis of legal rules, doctrines, and principles found in primary and secondary authorities, usually conducted within a law library.
A typographical convention used in NALT bibliographies to avoid repeating the author's name when citing multiple consecutive works by the same author.
The NALT committee that initially developed the Uniform Format and Citation Guide between 2013 and 2015.
A punctuation mark (…), with a space before and after, used to indicate that words or sentences have been omitted from a quotation.
Legal research that investigates law in operation within society using quantitative or qualitative empirical methodologies, surveys, or interviews.
In the context of a non-doctrinal research approach, this involves previous field or empirical studies, to be used to support an argument.
Abbreviation of Latin 'et alii' meaning 'and others.' In NALT footnotes, when a work has four or more authors, cite the first author followed by 'et al'.
A legal proceeding brought by one party without the presence or notification of other parties, commonly seen in interlocutory injunction applications.
The process where a scholar from another institution examines a research document, typically a postgraduate dissertation, before the oral defense.

An academic from another institution who assesses the research work, particularly at the postgraduate level. The external examiner is responsible for signing the certification page after a successful oral defence.
A prominent weekly Nigerian law report published by Nigerian Law Publications, covering judgments of the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal.
The first page of a research document, which is a blank page with no content or page number.
The NALT guide specifies that the font for the main body of the text should be Times New Roman, size 12, while footnotes should be size 10.
The official style of referencing adopted by NALT where citation indicators (superscript numbers) appear in the text and full source details are placed at the bottom of the page.

A method of referencing where sources are cited at the bottom of each page, with a superscript Arabic numeral in the text. Footnotes can be used to give plausible explanations of words or phrases without interrupting the flow of the main text. The NALT guide uses footnotes in the same way that OSCOLA does.
A referencing style that the NALT guide seeks to replace with its own indigenous citation style.
The use of historical sources to analyze a topic within a research project.

An abbreviation of the Latin word ibidem, meaning “in the same place,” which is used to refer to a source that was cited in the immediately preceding footnote. The NALT guide encourages cross-references instead of the use of ibid after an intervening source.
Abbreviation of Latin 'ibidem' meaning 'in the same place.' Used in NALT citations to refer to the immediately preceding source cited in the same footnote or prior footnote.
The NALT committee responsible for ensuring that the NALT manual is implemented in faculties of law nationwide. The committee is also responsible for updating the manual based on feedback.
The NALT committee responsible for monitoring the implementation of the Uniform Format and Citation Guide. This committee also receives feedback for the continuous improvement of the manual.
Latin term meaning 'in the matter of' or 'concerning.' Frequently used in the title of judicial proceedings where there are no adversarial parties, such as probate or bankruptcy.

A referencing style (used in APA) where the author's name and the year of publication are included in the main body of the text. The NALT guide does not use in-text citation; rather, it uses footnotes.
A formal lecture delivered by an academic upon appointment to a full professorship. NALT provides distinct citation rules specifying the university, inaugural lecture series number, and year.
Latin phrase meaning 'among other things.' Often used in legal commentary and briefs when summarizing portions of judicial reasoning.
A lecturer or academic staff member within the researcher's institution who assesses the research work. The internal examiner is responsible for signing the certification page.

A different source cited in a footnote that appears between the original citation of a source and subsequent citations of that same source. When an intervening source occurs, the NALT style requires the use of cross-references.
A font style that the NALT guide uses for case names, journal titles, and book titles. The ‘v’ in case citations should also be in italics.
A judicial decision that serves as an authority for deciding subsequent cases involving identical or similar points of law.
A list of important terms used in a research paper, presented in alphabetical order directly after the abstract.

glossary.term: Laws of the Federation of Nigeria (LFN)
glossary.definition: The official compilation of federal statutory enactments in Nigeria, currently cited primarily under the 2004 revision (e.g., Cap C23, LFN 2004).

A field of study concerning the research process in law, including research design, data collection, and analysis. The NALT manual was developed in part because of the lack of uniform teaching of legal research methodology across law faculties in Nigeria.
A list of abbreviated terms used in the research work, usually placed in the preliminary pages. Acronyms and abbreviations should be listed in alphabetical order.
An alphabetical list of all cases cited in the research work, placed in the preliminary pages.
An alphabetical list of all statutes, treaties and other international instruments cited in the research work, placed in the preliminary pages.
Latin term meaning 'place of standing.' The legal capacity or right of a party to bring an action before a court of law based on sufficient interest in the subject matter.
An undergraduate research dissertation required for the award of the LL.B degree. NALT Part Two sets the expected length at between 40 and 80 pages with a structured chapter layout.

A direct quotation that is longer than three lines. Long quotations should be indented from both the left and right margins without quotation marks, with a single line space before and after the quotation.
The NALT guide stipulates a 2.5cm margin on all sides of the A4 paper for research documents.
A core hallmark of the NALT citation format that discourages unnecessary full stops, particularly in acronyms, abbreviations (e.g., NWLR, LFN), and party connectors ('v').
A foreign style of referencing used in humanities and arts. The NALT guide adapts some of the principles of the MLA style, especially in the structuring of research writing.
A scholarly work, usually a detailed written study of a single specialized subject or an aspect of it. The NALT guide was first published as a monograph in 2019.
An association of law teachers in Nigeria that developed the Uniform Format and Citation Guide for Legal Research Writings in Nigeria.

glossary.term: NIALS (Nigerian Institute of Advanced Legal Studies)
glossary.definition: An institution that collaborated with NALT in the development and publication of the Uniform Format and Citation Guide.
A law reporting series specializing in judgments delivered by the Supreme Court of Nigeria on a quarterly basis.
Nigeria's most widely cited law reporting series, founded by Chief Gani Fawehinmi in 1985, published in parts and volumes.

A research approach that uses empirical data and socio-legal methods, such as surveys, questionnaires, and interviews, to analyse legal issues. It is also called the empirical or socio-legal approach.
Latin phrase meaning 'a saying by the way.' An expression of opinion or judicial remark made in a judgment that is not essential to the court's final decision and is not binding.

glossary.definition: Abbreviation of Latin 'opere citato' meaning 'in the work cited.' Used in academic writing to reference an earlier cited work with intervening citations.
The final stage of a postgraduate research project, where the candidate defends their work before a panel of examiners. The certifying statement will be redrafted after a successful oral defense.

The Oxford Standard for Citation of Legal Authorities. While widely used internationally, NALT was formulated to remedy OSCOLA's limitations in capturing Nigerian constitutional and judicial realities.

glossary.term: OSCOLA (Oxford Standard for Citation of Legal Authorities)
glossary.definition: A foreign style of referencing legal authorities. The NALT guide has adapted the OSCOLA citation style for its referencing, but replacing foreign examples with local ones, where possible.
The NALT guide adapted the OSCOLA style of referencing, while making it indigenous to the Nigerian legal system by replacing foreign examples and cases with Nigerian ones, where possible.
The NALT guide stipulates that page numbers should be placed at the bottom centre of the page.
The numbering of pages in a research document. In the NALT guide, the preliminary pages use Roman numerals, and the main body of the work uses Arabic numerals.
Latin term meaning 'scattered' or 'here and there,' indicating that a referenced matter is discussed continuously throughout a cited authority.

Scholarly publications that have been reviewed by experts in the field before publication. The NALT guide encourages students to use peer-reviewed journals over other sources, especially for literature reviews.
Latin term meaning 'through lack of care.' A judgment delivered in ignorance of an applicable statute or binding superior precedent, depriving it of binding authority.
The act of using someone else's work without proper attribution. Proper citation and referencing are necessary to avoid plagiarism.

The administrative unit in universities that is responsible for overseeing postgraduate studies. The NALT manual recommends that the Committee of Deans and Directors liaise with the PGS for full adoption and implementation of the NALT format.

The beginning section of a research work, containing items such as the title page, declaration page, certification page, dedication (optional), acknowledgements, table of contents, list of cases, list of statutes, list of acronyms, and abstract. The preliminaries are numbered in Roman numerals.
Latin phrase meaning 'at first sight.' Evidence that is sufficient to establish a fact or raise a presumption of fact unless rebutted or disproved.
Original legal documents such as constitutions, statutes, case law, and treaties. Primary sources state the law in its original form and are binding.
Terms used in the NALT guidelines to describe the causes of human trafficking.

The use of the exact words from a source. Short quotations are incorporated into the text, while longer quotations may be presented in a block format. Any errors in the original text should be indicated with [sic].
Latin phrase meaning 'the reason for the decision.' The legal principle or rationale upon which a court's final judgment is based, forming binding precedent.
Suggestions based on the findings of the research, which are usually presented in the concluding chapter.
Principles that guide the conduct of research, including informed consent, confidentiality, and avoiding plagiarism.
A testable statement that predicts the relationship between variables in a study, especially used in the non-doctrinal approach.
The principles and strategies that guide a researcher in gathering and analysing data. It includes the choice of research approach (doctrinal or non-doctrinal) and methods of data collection.
Specific, interrogative statements that are developed from the research problem and guide the research process. Research questions must be linked to the specific objectives of the research.
The number system (i, ii, iii, etc.) used to number the preliminary pages of a research work.
The boundaries of the research, including geographical coverage, content coverage, and subject matter.
Scholarly works that analyse and comment on primary sources, such as books, journal articles, and reviews. Secondary sources do not have binding authority but can be persuasive.
A direct quotation that is three lines or less in length. Short quotations should be enclosed in single quotation marks and integrated into the text of the document.
A Latin word used in square brackets [sic] to indicate that an error (such as a spelling mistake) appears in the original text of a quotation, and has not been introduced by the researcher.
The NALT guide specifies that research documents should be double-spaced. For abstracts, the text should be single-spaced, and not paragraphed.
Latin maxim 'stare decisis et non quieta movere' meaning 'to stand by things decided.' The foundational doctrine requiring inferior courts to follow decisions of superior courts.
A clear articulation of the issue or gap in knowledge that the research seeks to address.
Laws enacted by legislative bodies (federal, state, or local). The NALT guide specifies how to cite statutes, including the full title, year, and section numbers.
A form of subsidiary or delegated legislation enacted by ministers, regulatory agencies, or heads of court under authority delegated by an enabling primary statute.
Latin phrase meaning 'under judicial consideration.' Refers to a matter currently pending before a court, precluding public commentary that could prejudice proceedings.
A section in the conclusion of the research identifying potential areas for further research.
A brief overview of the key findings of the research, usually included in the concluding chapter.
Latin term meaning 'above.' Used in legal footnotes to cross-reference an authority or text cited earlier in the document.
A brief summary or overview of each chapter of a research work, highlighting the major contents.
A brief summary of the content of each chapter of a research document, often included in the first chapter.
A list of the chapters and sections of a research work, including page numbers.
The jurisprudential basis, theories, and principles that guide a field of study, used to justify how they apply to the research.

A long research paper submitted in partial fulfilment of an academic degree, especially at the postgraduate level. The NALT guide provides formatting guidelines for theses and dissertations at the master's and PhD levels.
The first page of a research work, which includes the title of the research, the author’s name, the institution, and the date of submission. No page number appears on the title page.
A verb used to describe a specific action or activity, often used to define research objectives.
Latin phrase meaning 'beyond the powers.' Describes acts performed beyond the constitutional or statutory authority granted to a public officer, corporation, or tribunal.
A judgment of a court of record that has not been officially published in any printed or electronic law report. NALT citation format requires the suit number and exact delivery date.

faqItems.question: What is the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: It is a manual developed by the Nigerian Association of Law Teachers (NALT) to provide a nationally approved uniform format and citation guide for legal research writing in Nigeria. It is intended for law faculties and legal research institutes in Nigeria.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The main purposes are to bridge existing gaps in research formats, facilitate a uniform approach to research writing and citation, facilitate the teaching of legal research methodology, and harmonise referencing styles across Nigerian law faculties. It also aims to provide an indigenous standard for legal research writing in Nigeria.

faqItems.question: Who is the intended audience of the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: It is intended for law faculties, legal research institutes, legal professionals, law teachers, and students in Nigeria.

faqItems.question: When was the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide developed and ratified?
faqItems.answer: The document was initiated at a NALT conference in January 2014 and finally ratified at the NALT's Conference in 2015.

faqItems.question: What are the main achievements of NALT regarding this guide?
faqItems.answer: The 'NALT Uniform Guide' is considered one of the main achievements of the Nigerian Association of Law Teachers since its inception and is a source of pride for the Association.

faqItems.question: How can I provide feedback or suggestions for improving the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: Suggestions, observations, and inputs for improvement can be forwarded to the NALT's Implementation Committee at naltguide2015@gmail.com.

faqItems.question: What are the general formatting guidelines for research writing under the NALT format?
faqItems.answer: This includes font (Times New Roman, size 12), double spacing (except for the abstract), using only one side of the paper, and adopting the NALT citation guide for footnotes.

faqItems.question: How should page numbers be formatted in research papers?
faqItems.answer: Preliminary pages (except the fly leaf and the title page, which is notionally page i) should be numbered with Roman numerals (ii, iii, iv) at the bottom center. The body of the text uses Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3...) also at the bottom center.

faqItems.question: How should chapter titles and subtitles be formatted?
faqItems.answer: Chapter titles should be in uppercase and centralized without a number. Main titles under the chapter title should be in uppercase with Arabic numerals. Sub-titles and sub-sub-titles use sub-Arabic numerals.

faqItems.question: What are the guidelines for writing an abstract?
faqItems.answer: The abstract should be one page, non-paragraphed, in the same font as the body but single-spaced. The word count should be 200-350 words for undergraduate essays and 500-600 words for master's dissertations and PhD theses. The abstract is usually written after the project's completion.

faqItems.question: How should undergraduate long essays and master's dissertations be structured in terms of chapters under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: The body is divided into five chapters, preceded by preliminaries and ending with a bibliography and appendices. Chapters One, Two, and Five are mandatory to structure the same way.

faqItems.question: How should PhD theses be structured in terms of chapters under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: The body is divided into six chapters, preceded by preliminaries and ending with a bibliography and appendices. Chapters One, Two, and Six are mandatory to structure the same way.

faqItems.question: How are Chapters Three and Four structured under the doctrinal approach for undergraduate and master's research?
faqItems.answer: The structuring of these chapters is at the discretion of the candidate, allowing for the distribution of their respective topics.

faqItems.question: How are Chapters Three, Four, and Five structured under the doctrinal approach for PhD research?
faqItems.answer: Candidates have these three chapters at their discretion to structure their topics under the guidance of their supervisors.

faqItems.question: What are the key differences in chapter structure between the doctrinal and non-doctrinal approaches?
faqItems.answer: Under the non-doctrinal approach, Chapter Three is devoted to data collection and research methodology, while Chapters Four and Five focus on data analysis, presentation of results, and discussions. Chapter Three under the doctrinal approach typically deals with the main topic of research.

faqItems.question: What citation style does the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide adopt?
faqItems.answer: The NALT format adapted the principles of the OSCOLA citation style as a guide.

faqItems.question: Where are citations placed in the text?
faqItems.answer: NALT adopts footnotes for citations within the text.

faqItems.question: What punctuation guidelines are used in NALT citations?
faqItems.answer: NALT's citation guide uses punctuation marks minimally, with no full stops after abbreviations (e.g., LFN, NWLR).

faqItems.question: How are case names cited under the NALT format?
faqItems.answer: 'v' (without a full stop) is used instead of 'versus' or 'vs'. Common words in case names can be abbreviated without a full stop (e.g., Co for Company). 'Re' is preferred over 'In Re'.

faqItems.question: How are different types of sources cited in footnotes according to the NALT guide?
faqItems.answer: The manual provides specimens for citing textbooks, journals, conference proceedings, newspapers, magazines, case reviews, online journals, and cases.

faqItems.question: How is the bibliography prepared under the NALT format?
faqItems.answer: The bibliography is a systematic listing of consulted works arranged alphabetically with author, title, volume/edition, publisher, and year of publication. Multiple works by the same author are listed together chronologically.

faqItems.question: What are the key differences between footnotes and the bibliography in the NALT style?
faqItems.answer: Footnotes record citations as written in the articles, while the bibliography has variations in author name order and might group works by the same author differently.

faqItems.question: What Latin expressions are abolished in the NALT citation style?
faqItems.answer: Supra, infra, ante, contra, id., op. cit., loc. cit., passim, et seq. have been abolished.

faqItems.question: How are subsequent citations and cross-references handled in the NALT style?
faqItems.answer: Cross-referencing using '(n...)' in brackets (where 'n' stands for 'note' and the number is the footnote where the information was first cited) is used in place of abolished Latin expressions. Ibid. can still be used to repeat a citation in the immediately preceding footnote if there is no intervening source.

faqItems.question: How should articles for journal publication be structured under the NALT format?
faqItems.answer: The body should be divided into no more than six main sections with Arabic numerals, followed by sub-titles and sub-sub-titles in a logical order. Main titles should be flushed to the left margin and in capital letters. Sub-subtitles are in small letters with each major word capitalized.

faqItems.question: What are the requirements for authors and abstracts in journal articles?
faqItems.answer: Articles must include the author(s)' names, followed by a symbol (*) with author information (degrees, post, affiliation, interests, email, phone) as footnotes on the first page. An abstract of 200-250 words should accompany all articles, titled "ABSTRACT" and flushed left, single-spaced, and not italicized.

faqItems.question: What other elements are required in articles for journal publication?
faqItems.answer: Keywords (not more than 5, alphabetical) under the abstract, a summary of findings, practicable recommendations, and a succinct conclusion using the word "findings" are required.

faqItems.question: What are the page length and formatting specifications for journal articles?
faqItems.answer: Articles should not be more than 15-20 pages (including abstract and footnotes), use Times New Roman font 12, 1.5 spacing, A4 paper with 2.5cm margins, and indented paragraphs. Footnotes should be in 10 font size, Times New Roman, and numbered serially with Arabic numerals.

faqItems.question: How should citations be formatted in journal articles?
faqItems.answer: All citations in journal articles must follow the NALT format structures and citation guide.

faqItems.question: Who developed the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The guide was developed by the NALT National Committee on Uniform Format for Legal Research and Citation Guide for Scholarly Writing, which worked between 2013 and 2015. The Nigerian Institute of Advanced Legal Studies (NIALS) was also involved in the formative stages, providing input through the NALT Draft Committee.

faqItems.question: When was the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide ratified and approved?
faqItems.answer: The document was ratified and approved at the NALT Conference held at Afe Babalola University (ABUAD) in 2015.

faqItems.question: Who is the intended audience for the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: This Manual is dedicated to law students' projects at all levels of the Faculties of Law across the nation and legal research institutes. It is also useful for academic legal researchers in their research activities, and for colleagues in full legal practice who write articles or review cases. The guide also caters to non-legal researchers in other disciplines, especially in Arts, Social Science, and Humanities.

faqItems.question: How does the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide compare to foreign citation guides like OSCOLA, MLA, and Bluebook?
faqItems.answer: The NALT's Guide has gone beyond the conventional citation guides offered by other manuals, such as OSCOLA (which is foreign). It is considered fuller, more detailed, wider in scope, and structurally logical than OSCOLA. Unlike foreign styles like OSCOLA, MLA, Bluebook, and APA, the NALT's Guide is designed to fully align with Nigerian legal research needs and 'Nigerianise' referencing. It explicitly spells out what students need to know about research project writing at all levels.

faqItems.question: What are the key areas covered by the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The Manual has three distinct areas divided into three major parts: 1. Students' project writing with examples on structuring research project topics. 2. The general style of referencing. 3. Article writing for journal publication in law. The second edition is divided into four parts, with Part One focusing on background information, Part Two on structuring research topics, Part Three on citation guidelines, and Part Four on journal article format.

faqItems.question: How does the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide address research writing at different academic levels?
faqItems.answer: The guide provides formats for structuring research topics for undergraduate long essays, master's theses, and PhD dissertations. It specifies the number of chapters and general guidelines for each level.

faqItems.question: What are the guidelines for structuring research topics into chapters according to the NALT format?
faqItems.answer: The breakdown of research topics into chapters and sub-divisions is of general application, whether doctrinal or non-doctrinal. For undergraduate and Master's dissertations under the doctrinal approach, the body is divided into five chapters, while a PhD thesis has six chapters. Chapters One, Two, and the final chapter (Five for undergraduate/Master's, Six for PhD) have mandatory structures and titles under the doctrinal approach. The guide also provides examples of how to structure chapters and assign titles and sub-titles.

faqItems.question: What are the two main approaches to legal research writing recognized by the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The two major acceptable approaches are the Doctrinal (Conceptual/Library-Based) Legal Research Approach and the Non-Doctrinal (Empirical/Socio-Legal) Legal Research Approach.

faqItems.question: How does the chapter structure differ between the doctrinal and non-doctrinal approaches for postgraduate research?
faqItems.answer: Under the doctrinal approach for PhD, Chapters One ("Introduction"), Two ("Conceptual and Theoretical Framework and Literature Review"), and Six ("Conclusion") are presented the same way by all students. Chapters Three to Five are at the candidate's discretion. Under the non-doctrinal approach, Chapters Two and Three are devoted to Literature Review and Research Methodology, respectively. Chapters Four and Five focus on research analysis and data presentation, while Chapter Six remains the "Conclusion". Chapter One in the non-doctrinal approach also includes a Research Hypothesis.

faqItems.question: What are some general guidelines for research writing according to the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: Guidelines include specifications for page limits, font (Times New Roman, size 12), double spacing, one side of paper for typing, adoption of NALT citation for footnotes, and preparation of a bibliography. It also specifies requirements for the abstract (one page, non-paragraphed, with word limits varying by degree). Pagination uses Roman numerals for preliminaries and Arabic numerals for the main body. Specific margin specifications are also provided.

faqItems.question: What are the NALT citation guidelines for footnotes?
faqItems.answer: NALT's citation guide uses punctuation marks minimally, with no full stops after abbreviations (e.g., LFN, FWLR). It uses 'v' without a full stop for 'versus' in case citations. A comma is used to separate the author's name from the work title. A colon (:) separates a title from a subtitle. Superscript numbers are used as footnote markers within the text, with corresponding footnotes at the bottom of the page. 'Ibid.' can be used to repeat a citation in the immediately preceding footnote, and '(n…)' for cross-referencing to a previously cited source.

faqItems.question: How should quotations be formatted according to the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: Short quotations are incorporated into the text within single quotation marks. Long quotations (longer than 3 lines/40 words) should be indented in a block format from both sides, with no quotation marks. An ellipsis (...) is used to indicate omitted text. If emphasis is added to a quotation, (emphasis added) should be indicated in brackets.

faqItems.question: What are the guidelines for preparing a bibliography according to the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The bibliography is a systematic listing of all published works consulted, whether cited in the main body or not, arranged in alphabetical order by the author's surname. In the bibliography, entries start with the author's surname, whereas footnotes reproduce the name exactly as it appears in the source.

faqItems.question: What format does the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide recommend for articles in journals?
faqItems.answer: Articles should be divided into sections of sub-main titles (not more than six), assigned Arabic numerals, followed by sub-titles and sub-sub-titles in a logical order. Sub-main titles are in capital letters and flushed to the left margin. Sub-subtitles are in small letters with initial capitals. An abstract (200-250 words) and keywords should accompany all articles. The citation of sources in journal articles should be in footnotes using the NALT format. Pages should not exceed 15-20.

faqItems.question: How can the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide be implemented and adopted by law faculties in Nigeria?
faqItems.answer: Deans and Directors of Law Faculties are urged to integrate this Manual into their local settings at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels and in technical legal writing. They should set up committees within their faculties to review the Manual, identify relevant areas for adoption, and make recommendations to Postgraduate Schools (PGS). NALT's EXCO must work closely with the Committee of Deans and Directors to officially recommend the Manual to their respective PGS.

faqItems.question: What are some of the challenges in achieving full acceptance and implementation of the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: One major challenge is the limited availability of hard copies, which has restricted access to the Manual's content. Another challenge is that Deans and Directors of Law Faculties have yet to take an active role in implementing this standardised approach. Some faculties have also derailed from its application.

faqItems.question: What efforts are being made to promote and disseminate the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The Manual has been given wide publicity through advocacy and dissemination by individuals and groups within NALT through seminars at various institutions. Publishing the Manual as a monograph is also aimed at enhancing dissemination and access.

faqItems.question: Is the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide intended to be a static document, or will it be updated?
faqItems.answer: The review of the Manual is a continuous process until a robust desired result is reached. Colleagues are encouraged to observe shortfalls, make useful and constructive suggestions, and generate new ideas for improvements. Suggestions can be forwarded to the NALT's Implementation Committee.

faqItems.question: Has the Council of Legal Education (CLE) endorsed the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: There is a hope and recommendation that the Council of Legal Education (CLE) will endorse this document as part of the compulsory legal education collection for the accreditation of law courses. NALT is urged to pass a resolution urging the CLE to give it statutory backing.

faqItems.question: Where can one find more detailed information or specimens for citation using the NALT format?
faqItems.answer: Part Three of the Manual provides NALT Citation Guidelines for Style of Referencing, including a quick summary and specimens for footnotes citation for various sources.

faqItems.question: What are the key differences between footnotes and bibliography in the NALT style?
faqItems.answer: In footnotes, citations are recorded the way they are written in the articles, while in the bibliography, entries start with the author's surname. A reference contains only works cited, while a bibliography contains all materials consulted.

faqItems.question: What are the roles of the NALT Monitoring Committee and the Committee of Deans and Directors in relation to the guide?
faqItems.answer: The NALT Monitoring Committee has been involved in advocacy and dissemination of the Manual. NALT's EXCO needs to work closely with the Committee of Deans and Directors to ensure proper implementation by officially recommending the Manual. The Committee is also meant to receive feedback for evaluation and improvement.

faqItems.question: What are the expected minimum and maximum page lengths for undergraduate long essays?
faqItems.answer: The minimum page length for an undergraduate long essay is 40 pages, and the maximum is 80 pages.

faqItems.question: What are the expected minimum and maximum page lengths for Master's dissertations?
faqItems.answer: The minimum page length for a Master's dissertation is 80 pages, and the maximum is 150 pages.

faqItems.question: What are the expected minimum and maximum page lengths for PhD theses?
faqItems.answer: The minimum page length for a PhD thesis is 200 pages, and the maximum is 400 pages. The PhD thesis is also expected to be divided into six (6) chapters.

faqItems.question: What font and font size should be used for research writing?
faqItems.answer: The recommended font is Times New Roman with a font size of 12.

faqItems.question: What line spacing should be used for research writing?
faqItems.answer: Double spacing should be used for typing the dissertation/thesis. Abstracts, however, use single line spacing.

faqItems.question: Should both sides of the paper be used for typing?
faqItems.answer: Only one side of the paper should be used for typing.

faqItems.question: What citation guide should be adopted within the text?
faqItems.answer: The NALT citation guide for footnotes shall be adopted within the text.

faqItems.question: Are students expected to prepare a bibliography?
faqItems.answer: Yes, students are expected to prepare a list of bibliography of sources consulted.

faqItems.question: Who is expected to undergo an external oral examination?
faqItems.answer: Only postgraduate (PG) students are expected to undergo an external oral examination in defense of their dissertations and PhD theses.

faqItems.question: Is an abstract required?
faqItems.answer: What is the expected length? Yes, all students are expected to write an abstract.

faqItems.question: Should the abstract be paragraphed?
faqItems.answer: No, the abstract should be non-paragraphed.

faqItems.question: How should the pages of the research work be numbered?
faqItems.answer: Preliminary pages are numbered in Roman numerals (i, ii, iii, etc.), while Arabic numerals (1, 2, 3, etc.) are used to number the main body of the work (from chapter one to bibliography/appendices). The title page does not indicate a page number, though it is considered page i.

faqItems.question: What is the recommended paper color, quality, and size?
faqItems.answer: White paper of good quality and size A4 is recommended.

faqItems.question: How many chapters should the body of an undergraduate long essay be divided into?
faqItems.answer: The body of a long essay is divided into five chapters.

faqItems.question: What precedes and follows the body of the undergraduate long essay?
faqItems.answer: The chapters are preceded by preliminaries and end with bibliography and appendices (if any).

faqItems.question: Are chapter titles required for each chapter?
faqItems.answer: Yes, there must be a chapter title for each chapter from chapters one to five.

faqItems.question: What citation style should be adopted in the text of an undergraduate long essay?
faqItems.answer: NALT's Footnotes shall be adopted in-text.

faqItems.question: Is an abstract required for an undergraduate long essay?
faqItems.answer: What is the word limit? Yes, all students are expected to write a non-paragraphed abstract of one page. The entire abstract should not be more than 200-350 words.

faqItems.question: How many chapters should the body of a Master's dissertation be divided into?
faqItems.answer: The body of the essay is divided into five (5) chapters.

faqItems.question: What is the minimum and maximum page length for a Master's dissertation?
faqItems.answer: 100 pages minimum and 150 pages maximum.

faqItems.question: Are the structuring approaches similar to undergraduate research?
faqItems.answer: Yes, the general rules apply, and the approaches are similar to the structuring in undergraduate research.

faqItems.question: How many chapters should the body of a PhD thesis be divided into?
faqItems.answer: The body of a PhD thesis is divided into six (6) chapters.

faqItems.question: What precedes and follows the chapters of a PhD thesis?
faqItems.answer: The chapters are also preceded by the preliminaries and end with the bibliography and appendices (if any).

faqItems.question: What is the minimum and maximum page length for a PhD thesis?
faqItems.answer: 200 pages minimum and 400 pages maximum, depending on the choice of topic.

faqItems.question: Is an abstract required for a PhD thesis?
faqItems.answer: What is the word limit? Yes, students are expected to write a non-paragraphed abstract of one page. The entire abstract should not be more than 500-600 words.

faqItems.question: When is the abstract usually written?
faqItems.answer: The abstract is usually written after the completion of the project.

faqItems.question: Under the doctrinal approach, which chapters have the same titles for all students?
faqItems.answer: What are these titles? Under the doctrinal approach, chapters one (1), two (2), and six (6) (the final chapter for a PhD) are presented the same way by all students.

faqItems.question: Under the non-doctrinal approach, what are chapters two and three devoted to?
faqItems.answer: Under the non-doctrinal approach, chapters two and three are devoted to Literature Review and Research Methodology, respectively.

faqItems.question: Under the non-doctrinal approach, what are chapters four and five devoted to?
faqItems.answer: Chapters four and five are devoted to research analysis and data presentation.

faqItems.question: Under the non-doctrinal approach, what is chapter six titled?
faqItems.answer: Chapter six remains the same as under the doctrinal approach and is titled "Conclusion".

faqItems.question: What are the three major areas of focus for preliminaries?
faqItems.answer: The three major areas are: 1. The general preliminaries, 2. The abstract, and 3. Bibliography/appendix.

faqItems.question: How are the parts of preliminaries numbered?
faqItems.answer: The parts of preliminaries are numbered in Roman numerals.

faqItems.question: In what case should the titles of the preliminaries and items in the title page and table of contents be written?
faqItems.answer: All titles of the preliminaries and all the items in the title page and the table of contents are to be written in uppercase (capital or block letters).

faqItems.question: Are preliminaries, bibliography, and appendices applicable to both undergraduate and postgraduate research projects?
faqItems.answer: Yes, with some varying degrees in application.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of an abstract?
faqItems.answer: An abstract gives a concise summary of the body of text or thesis. It helps researchers to present a quick and general overview of the contents of a subject matter.

faqItems.question: Is an abstract a chapter-by-chapter review?
faqItems.answer: No, an abstract is not a chapter-by-chapter review.

faqItems.question: In what format should an abstract be written?
faqItems.answer: It is the summary of the entire work written in an un-paragraphed block.

faqItems.question: Where is the bibliography presented?
faqItems.answer: Bibliography is presented at the end of the whole exercise.

faqItems.question: How should the bibliography be titled?
faqItems.answer: It is titled 'BIBLIOGRAPHY' on a separate page.

faqItems.question: What information does a bibliography contain?
faqItems.answer: It lists all materials consulted, whether expressly cited in the main body or not.

faqItems.question: How does a reference differ from a bibliography?
faqItems.answer: A reference contains only the works cited or quoted verbatim in the text, while a bibliography contains all materials consulted.

faqItems.question: What is an appendix?
faqItems.answer: An appendix represents some data or information in the form of tables, charts, and other materials which, although important, the researcher does not want to include in the main body.

faqItems.question: Where are appendices placed?
faqItems.answer: These are placed at the end or attached to the main body of the research report.

faqItems.question: What are the two major acceptable approaches to legal research writing in Nigerian law faculties?
faqItems.answer: The two major acceptable approaches are: Doctrinal (Conceptual/Library-Based) Legal Research Approach and Non-Doctrinal (Empirical/Socio-Legal) Legal Research Approach.

faqItems.question: What are some other names for the doctrinal research approach?
faqItems.answer: It is variously called library-based research, pure theoretical research, legal dogmatic, black letter law research, or ‘arm-chair’ research.

faqItems.question: What does the doctrinal research approach involve?
faqItems.answer: It involves the interpretation, descriptive analysis, and systematization of legal norms or doctrine.

faqItems.question: Is the doctrinal research approach based on empirical statistical analysis?
faqItems.answer: No, this research approach is not based on empirical statistical analysis.

faqItems.question: What type of research methods does the doctrinal approach use?
faqItems.answer: It uses qualitative research methods (as opposed to quantitative methods).

faqItems.question: How many chapters are research topics under the doctrinal approach divided into for undergraduate long essays and Master's dissertations?
faqItems.answer: They are divided into five chapters.

faqItems.question: How many chapters are research topics under the doctrinal approach divided into for a PhD thesis?
faqItems.answer: A PhD thesis is divided into six chapters, and this is mandatory.

faqItems.question: Under the doctrinal approach, which chapters are mandatory for all candidates to structure their project topics in the same way?
faqItems.answer: Chapters One, Two, and Five (for Master's) or Six (for PhD) are mandatory.

faqItems.question: What is typically the title of Chapter One under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: INTRODUCTION.

faqItems.question: What is typically the title of Chapter Two under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: CONCEPTUAL, THEORETICAL FRAMEWORKS AND LITERATURE REVIEW.

faqItems.question: From which chapter are students advised to start addressing their main topics under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: Students are advised to start addressing their main topics from Chapter 3.

faqItems.question: What could Chapter Three focus on under the doctrinal approach (using the example of Human Trafficking)?
faqItems.answer: It could focus on the International and National Legal Framework Against Human Trafficking.

faqItems.question: What could Chapter Four focus on under the doctrinal approach (using the example of Human Trafficking)?
faqItems.answer: It could be assigned a different but relevant topic, such as HUMAN TRAFFICKING IN NIGERIA: CAUSES AND EFFECTS.

faqItems.question: What is the title of Chapter Five for a Master's dissertation under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: CONCLUSION.

faqItems.question: What information does the final chapter (Five for Master's, Six for PhD) typically contain under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: It contains the summary of findings, recommendations, contribution to knowledge, suggested areas for further studies, and conclusion.

faqItems.question: What should Chapter One (Introduction) provide?
faqItems.answer: It should provide a general background to the subject matter.

faqItems.question: What should the statement of the problem be supported by?
faqItems.answer: As much as possible, the problem should be supported by some empirical, theoretical, and practical evidence.

faqItems.question: What is the relationship between research questions and research objectives?
faqItems.answer: Research questions emanate from or are linked with the specific objectives of the research. There is a direct link between research questions and research objectives in terms of both substance and number.

faqItems.question: What are the three dimensions of the scope of the study?
faqItems.answer: The scope has three dimensions: geographical coverage, content coverage, and subject matter coverage.

faqItems.question: What does the limitation of the study refer to?
faqItems.answer: This has to do with the shortcomings, difficulties, challenges, or constraints encountered in designing and conducting the research.

faqItems.question: What should the significance of the study explain?
faqItems.answer: It should explain the relevance and value of the research.

faqItems.question: What does the research approach/methodology part consist of?
faqItems.answer: This part consists of the research approaches (whether doctrinal and/or non-doctrinal) and method(s) of data collection.

faqItems.question: What should the synopsis of the chapters highlight?
faqItems.answer: This part highlights the major contents of each chapter.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Two (Conceptual, Theoretical Frameworks and Literature Review) typically address under "Conceptual Clarification"?
faqItems.answer: This addresses the issues, nature, or principles associated with a research topic. It is an elaboration or definition of the major words of the topic of the work.

faqItems.question: What does the "Theoretical Framework" in Chapter Two include?
faqItems.answer: This includes historical foundations as well as the principles and ideas upon which the research topic is premised and such other preliminaries relevant to the chosen topic.

faqItems.question: What is the purpose of the "Literature Review" in Chapter Two?
faqItems.answer: It discusses written or published related literature or works on opinions of authorities and/or on results of previous studies.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Three typically involve under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: It is the re-statement of the main research topic or the subject matter of research for thorough examination and critical analysis.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Four often address under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: This chapter could be a continuation of the topic or subject matter under Chapter Three, addressing the application and enforcement of the topic under discussion, as well as the problems and challenges associated with the research topic.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Five (for Master's) or Chapter Six (for PhD) contain under the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: This final chapter contains a summary of findings, recommendations, contribution to knowledge, suggested areas for further studies, and conclusion.

faqItems.question: How should the Bibliography and Appendices be presented at the end?
faqItems.answer: These are presented at the end of the entire work, with the heading 'BIBLIOGRAPHY' written separately from the final chapter and on a fresh page. Appendices (if any) are also placed on separate page(s) after the bibliography.

faqItems.question: What is the non-doctrinal approach to research writing also known as?
faqItems.answer: This is the scientific approach to empirical investigation and scientific data collection.

faqItems.question: What does the non-doctrinal approach adopt?
faqItems.answer: The non-doctrinal approach adopts an empirical approach through fieldwork.

faqItems.question: What are some methods of research under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: Methods include research designs, population sampling, and the use of research techniques such as interviews with structured/unstructured questionnaires, and experimental designs with observations.

faqItems.question: What is the data analysis method under the non-doctrinal approach referred to as?
faqItems.answer: It is basically referred to as quantitative analysis.

faqItems.question: What is generated in non-doctrinal research that will be verified at the end?
faqItems.answer: In non-doctrinal research, a hypothesis is generated.

faqItems.question: How many chapters do both approaches typically contain?
faqItems.answer: Both approaches contain six chapters, with a similar structure as obtained under the doctrinal approach.

faqItems.question: Which chapter under the non-doctrinal approach has features similar to the doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: Chapter One.

faqItems.question: Which chapters are the same under both approaches, with few differences?
faqItems.answer: Chapters One and Six.

faqItems.question: What is Chapter Two devoted to under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: It is devoted to literature review, theoretical and conceptual frameworks of the subject matter of research.

faqItems.question: What is Chapter Three devoted to under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: It is devoted to data collection and research methodology.

faqItems.question: What are Chapters Four and Five devoted to under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: They are devoted to data analysis, presentation of results, and discussions.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Five contain under the doctrinal approach (that differs from non-doctrinal)?
faqItems.answer: It contains critical analysis and examination of challenges associated with the chosen research topic.

faqItems.question: What is typically the title of Chapter One?
faqItems.answer: INTRODUCTION.

faqItems.question: What is typically the title of Chapter Two?
faqItems.answer: CONCEPTUAL AND THEORETICAL FRAMEWORK & LITERATURE REVIEW.

faqItems.question: What would Chapter Three focus on under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: Chapter Three would focus on Research Methodology (not explicitly titled in this section but implied as a key difference).

faqItems.question: What is the title of the final chapter under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: CONCLUSION.

faqItems.question: To whom is the information on the non-doctrinal approach applicable?
faqItems.answer: This information is applicable only to Master and PhD Candidates who desire to carry out empirical legal research using the non-doctrinal approach.

faqItems.question: What is crucial to project writing at all levels under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: Chapter One: Introduction is crucial.

faqItems.question: What does the statement of the problem require under the non-doctrinal approach?
faqItems.answer: It requires empirical, theoretical, and practical evidence.

faqItems.question: What is the "Purpose of the Study" generally referred to as?
faqItems.answer: It is generally referred to as the aim and objectives of the study.

faqItems.question: What are hypotheses?
faqItems.answer: A hypothesis is a preliminary assumption or tentative explanation that accounts for a set of facts.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Two under the non-doctrinal approach contain?
faqItems.answer: It contains the theoretical framework, conceptual framework, and empirical framework of previous field or empirical studies, as well as a summary of the review of relevant/related literature and gap in knowledge.

faqItems.question: What does Chapter Three (Research Methodology) under the non-doctrinal approach contain?
faqItems.answer: It contains information on data collection and research design, population, sample and sampling techniques, instrument for data collection, validation and reliability of the instrument, method of data collection, and method of data analysis.

faqItems.question: What do Chapters Four and Five under the non-doctrinal approach focus on?
faqItems.answer: They focus on data presentation and results and discussion, including comparison with existing literature, resolution of the original problem, and implications of findings.

faqItems.question: What does the final chapter (Conclusion) under the non-doctrinal approach contain?
faqItems.answer: It contains a summary of findings, recommendations, suggestions for further studies/research, contribution to knowledge, and conclusive remarks.

faqItems.question: How are the Bibliography and Appendices presented in non-doctrinal research?
faqItems.answer: These are presented at the end with no numbering assigned to them. The bibliography is a chronological alphabetical listing, and appendices contain instruments like questionnaires and statistical tables.

faqItems.question: What is the fundamental approach to referencing adopted by the NALT Citation Guide?
faqItems.answer: The NALT Uniform Citation Guide adapts and operates with the ‘Footnotes’ style of referencing. This means that Arabic numerals are used in superscript in the body of the essay to identify sources. Every source cited must be reflected at the foot of each page with the corresponding Arabic numeral, providing full citation information at a glance.

faqItems.question: Why was the 'Footnotes' style chosen by NALT?
faqItems.answer: The choice of footnotes was informed by the advantages they offer to legal writing. Besides citing various sources like cases, journal articles, and textbooks, footnotes can also be used to refer readers to plausible explanations of legal sources, foreign or Latin maxims, or additional information without interrupting the flow of the main text.

faqItems.question: What are the general punctuation rules in NALT citation?
faqItems.answer: NALT's citation guide uses punctuation marks minimally. For example, no full stops come after abbreviations.

faqItems.question: How are case names punctuated when cited?
faqItems.answer: In citing cases, ‘v’ (without a full stop) is used in place of ‘versus’ or ‘vs’ for the parties' names. Also, no full stops are used in the abbreviation of the title of the law report and the part of the law report. Case names should be in italics and (except for the first letters of the names) in lower case, including the ‘v’.

faqItems.question: How should multiple citations in a single footnote be separated?
faqItems.answer: Where more than one citation is given in a single footnote, they should be separated by semi-colons (;).

faqItems.question: What punctuation is used to separate the author's name from the title of a work?
faqItems.answer: In making reference to a book, a journal article, etc., a comma (,) is used to separate the name of the author(s) from the title of the work.

faqItems.question: How should online sources be cited under NALT style?
faqItems.answer: If a publication is sourced online but is also available in hard copy, cite the hard copy details. If it is exclusively online, add the web address and the date of last access.

faqItems.question: What punctuation is used between a title and a subtitle?
faqItems.answer: A colon (:) is used to separate a title from a subtitle. The researcher can insert the colon even if the original source does not have one.

faqItems.question: How is the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 cited?
faqItems.answer: In the first instance, the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 should be cited in full, with the words ‘as amended’ attached. Subsequently, it may be cited by way of acronym, i.e., CFRN 1999 (as amended); or by some other descriptive words such as ‘the 1999 Constitution’.

faqItems.question: What are the rules for citing statutes under NALT style?
faqItems.answer: Statutes should be cited by their short titles (as indicated in the statutes themselves), using capitals for the first letter of principal words. The first instance of citation should be in full. Subsequently, acronyms or descriptive words can be used, provided they are clearly defined. The word ‘Act’ (and by extension, ‘Law’, ‘Rule’, ‘Treaty’, etc.) must appear in full as a separate word. When cited in a footnote, statutes should be cited in full as codified.

faqItems.question: How should Rules of Court and Practice Directions be cited?
faqItems.answer: Rules of Court and Practice Directions should be cited in accordance with their titles, including their years of making.

faqItems.question: What are the abbreviations for parts, sections, subsections, and paragraphs?
faqItems.answer: The following abbreviations are used, preferably in footnotes: Part/Parts (pt/pts), Section/Sections (s/ss), Subsection/Subsections (sub-s/sub-ss), Paragraph/Paragraphs (para/paras), Schedule/Schedules (sch/schs).

faqItems.question: How are textbooks cited in footnotes?
faqItems.answer: For authored books, cite the author’s name exactly as it appears in the publication, omitting prefixes or titles. For up to three authors, insert ‘and’ between their names. For more than three authors, give the details of the first author and add ‘and others’. Then include the title of the book in italics, followed by the edition (if applicable), publisher, and year of publication. Page numbers should be included if referring to a specific page.

faqItems.question: How are articles in journals cited in footnotes?
faqItems.answer: Cite the author's name, the title of the article in single quotation marks, the name of the journal in italics, the year in brackets, the volume and issue number (if applicable), and the page number(s). For online journals, add the web address and date of last access.

faqItems.question: How are conference proceedings cited?
faqItems.answer: List the author(s), the title of the paper in single quotation marks, the name of the conference proceedings in italics (if applicable), the year of the conference in brackets, and the page range. You may also include the full name of the conference, place, and dates.

faqItems.question: How are newspapers and magazines cited?
faqItems.answer: Cite the author, the title of the article in single quotation marks, the name of the newspaper/magazine in italics, the city of publication in brackets, the day month year of publication, and the page number(s). If it is an editorial, cite ‘Editorial’ as the author. For online versions, provide the web address and date of access if no page number is available.

faqItems.question: How are projects, master’s dissertations, and PhD theses cited?
faqItems.answer: Cite the author, the title of the work in italics, the type of academic work in brackets (e.g., LLM Dissertation, PhD Thesis), the Faculty, the University, and the year.

faqItems.question: How are inaugural lectures and distinguished lecture series cited?
faqItems.answer: The title should be italicised like a book, followed by the occasion, place, and date in brackets.

faqItems.question: What are citation signals and how are they used?
faqItems.answer: Whenever information is quoted, paraphrased, or an idea is presented, a superscript number (citation indicator) is inserted after the information or the author's name. This number is replicated at the foot of the page with the full citation. Footnotes can also be used for clarification or additional information.

faqItems.question: What are the rules for direct quotations?
faqItems.answer: Short quotations (not more than three lines) should be incorporated into the main text and enclosed in single quotation marks. Longer quotations should be indented on both sides without quotation marks, with a single-line space before and after.

faqItems.question: What is a bibliography and what information does it contain?
faqItems.answer: A bibliography is a systematic listing of all published works consulted by the researcher, arranged in a specific or alphabetical order. It contains information such as author, title, volume/edition, publisher, and year of publication. The bibliography is typically placed after the main body of the work.

blogs.title: Addressing the Limitations of Foreign Citation Styles in Nigerian Legal Research (OSCOLA, MLA, APA)
blogs.author: NALT Cite Editorial Team
blogs.excerpt: Addressing the Limitations of Foreign Citation Styles in Nigerian Legal Research (OSCOLA, MLA, APA)
blogs.content:
Addressing the Limitations of Foreign Citation Styles in Nigerian Legal Research (OSCOLA, MLA, APA)

For a long time, legal research and writing in Nigeria relied heavily on foreign citation styles such as OSCOLA (Oxford Standard for Citation of Legal Authorities), MLA (Modern Language Association), and APA (American Psychological Association). While these styles have their merits, the Nigerian Association of Law Teachers (NALT) recognized their inherent limitations in fully addressing the unique needs of legal scholarship within the Nigerian context. This blog post will delve into these limitations, drawing upon the insights provided by the NALT Uniform Format and Citation Guide for Legal Research Writing in Nigeria (NALT's Blue Book Basic Guide).

The Prevalent Use and Inadequacies of Foreign Styles:

Before the advent of the NALT's guide, Nigerian Law Faculties adopted these foreign citation and structure styles based largely on author or institutional preference. This resulted in a lack of a consensus citation format, creating challenges for editors of journals and conference proceedings and complicating the assessment of postgraduate research by external supervisors who had to grapple with various writing styles.

The NALT's research highlighted that these foreign styles, including OSCOLA, MLA, Bluebook, and APA, failed to adequately accommodate local issues in legal research writing. These styles came with limitations that did not fully align with Nigerian legal research needs.

Specific Limitations of Foreign Styles:

OSCOLA: While OSCOLA became a widely used authority for citing legal materials in many Nigerian law faculties, its primary focus is on the citation of legal authorities, particularly within the UK legal system. The NALT guide points out that Nigeria, despite being a Commonwealth nation, has remarkable differences in its statutory provisions, limiting OSCOLA's direct applicability. Furthermore, OSCOLA does not comprehensively address the structuring of legal research writing, such as undergraduate and postgraduate projects or legal journal articles.

MLA: Originally developed for research writing in English and Literature, MLA, while flexible and using footnotes, was not specifically designed for the nuances of legal citation and the Nigerian legal context.

APA: The APA style, primarily used in the social sciences, employs endnotes for compiling reference materials, unlike the footnote style favored in legal scholarship and adopted by the NALT guide (similar to OSCOLA). This difference in referencing style can disrupt the flow of legal arguments where immediate reference and explanation are often necessary.

The NALT Solution: A Localized and Comprehensive Guide:

Recognizing these shortcomings, the NALT embarked on creating its own customised standard format and reference guide in legal research writing in Nigeria. The NALT's Uniform Format and Citation Guide was conceived to be fuller, more detailed, wider in scope, and structurally logical compared to foreign manuals like OSCOLA.

Key Features Addressing the Limitations:

Nigerian Contextualization: The NALT guide explicitly aims to 'Nigerianise' referencing by replacing foreign cases, statutes, rules, and regulations with local ones where possible for user-friendliness. It also encourages the use of local academic authors as illustrations.

Comprehensive Scope: Unlike OSCOLA's primary focus on citation, the NALT guide is all-encompassing. It provides guidance not only on citation but also on the formation and structuring of research topics for all levels of academic work, from undergraduate essays to PhD theses. It also includes a dedicated section on the format for articles in journal publication.

Uniformity and Coherence: A central goal of the NALT guide is to achieve uniform and standardised formats and styles of referencing across Law Faculties in Nigerian Universities. This addresses the pre-existing lack of consensus and aims to facilitate easier assessment and a more coherent body of Nigerian legal scholarship.

Adaptation and Localization: While the NALT guide draws inspiration from the principles, features, and technicalities of MLA and OSCOLA, it localizes these elements to make them user-friendly within the Nigerian setting. For instance, it adopts the footnote style of referencing similar to OSCOLA.

Conclusion:

The NALT's Uniform Format and Citation Guide represents a significant step towards strengthening legal education and research in Nigeria. By directly addressing the limitations of foreign citation styles in accommodating the local legal landscape and the broader needs of legal research writing, the NALT has provided an indigenous and comprehensive framework designed to foster uniformity, coherence, and relevance in Nigerian legal scholarship. The adoption of this guide promises to elevate the quality and impact of legal research emanating from Nigerian tertiary institutions.

NALT Citation Guide: Writing a Strong Conclusion for Your Legal Research

This post, continuing our exploration of the Nigerian Association of Law Teachers (NALT) Uniform Format and Citation Guide, focuses on crafting a compelling and effective concluding chapter for your legal research in Nigeria. Whether you are writing an undergraduate long essay, a master's dissertation, or a PhD thesis, the final chapter is your opportunity to summarize your key findings, offer insightful recommendations, and articulate the significance of your work.

The Purpose of the Concluding Chapter

The concluding chapter, typically Chapter Five for undergraduate and master's dissertations and Chapter Six for PhD theses, serves as the final statement of your research. It should not introduce new information but rather synthesize and reflect upon the analysis presented in the preceding chapters. According to the NALT manual, these final chapters are prepared in a similar manner under both doctrinal and non-doctrinal research approaches.

Key Elements of a Strong Conclusion

The NALT guide outlines several essential components that should be included in your concluding chapter:

Summary of Findings: This section should provide a concise overview of the most important discoveries and insights that emerged from your research. It should directly relate back to your research questions or hypotheses and highlight the key arguments you have developed throughout your work.

Recommendations: Based directly on your findings, this section should offer practicable and realistic suggestions to address the problems or issues you have identified in your research. The NALT manual specifically advises against making unrealistic recommendations. Ensure that each recommendation is logically derived from your analysis.

Contributions to Knowledge: Here, you should explicitly state the specific ways in which your research contributes to the existing body of knowledge in your field of law. This might include offering a new perspective, filling a gap in the literature, challenging existing assumptions, or providing empirical evidence to support or refute established theories.

Suggested Areas for Further Studies: This section looks forward, identifying potential avenues for future research that could build upon or extend the findings of your work. This demonstrates a broader understanding of the research landscape and can inspire further scholarly inquiry.

Conclusion (Conclusive Remarks): This is the final part of the chapter, offering succinct concluding remarks that bring your entire research exercise to a close. The NALT guide suggests keeping this section to no more than half a page or two to three paragraphs. It should reiterate your main arguments and leave the reader with a clear understanding of the significance and implications of your research.

Connecting Back to Your Research Objectives

A strong conclusion effectively ties together all the threads of your research. Ensure that your summary of findings directly answers your initial research questions and that your recommendations are aligned with your research objectives. The concluding chapter should provide a sense of closure and coherence, demonstrating that you have successfully addressed the scope of your study as defined in your introductory chapter.

Final Touches

Remember that, according to the NALT guide, every chapter starts on a fresh page, including your concluding chapter. Ensure that you maintain consistency in formatting, including font type and size, as outlined in Part Two of the manual. While citations are crucial throughout your research, the concluding chapter primarily summarizes and reflects, so the focus should be on the clarity and strength of your own analysis and insights.

By diligently crafting a well-structured and thoughtful concluding chapter, you will leave a lasting impression on your readers and effectively communicate the value and impact of your Nigerian legal research within the framework of the NALT Citation Guide.
